levels.name: abstract specification
levels.obligation: States the operation and its normative properties independently of any implementation.
levels.artefact: the normative source (RFC, FIPS, or the project constitution) named by the requirement node

levels.name: executable reference
levels.obligation: An executable implementation of the abstract specification that the Rust implementation can be compared against.
levels.artefact: an independently written reference program and its conformance run

levels.name: Rust implementation
levels.obligation: The crate under src/ implements the reference's observable behaviour and its safe interior enforces the memory-safety invariants.
levels.artefact: the tracked src/ tree at the candidate

levels.name: ABI contract
levels.obligation: The observable C surface matches the authority: exported symbols and versions, repr(C) layouts, ownership, error-queue behaviour and callback semantics.

levels.name: machine code
levels.obligation: The exact compiled artefact implements the ABI contract and preserves the verified source properties.
levels.artefact: the DSO digests recorded by evidence/etp2/reproducibility.json

levels.name: consumer composition
levels.obligation: For every reachable call site c in the loaded DSO, Pre(c) implies the kernel precondition P, and Q satisfies the next consumer.

edges.obligation: The executable reference implements every normative statement of the abstract specification, for the declared input population, and is independent of the Rust implementation.
edges.invalidation_rule: A change to the abstract specification, the reference, or the ETP-T5 conformance tool invalidates the discharge; a new candidate requires a new reference run.
edges.does_not_establish: A proof about the abstract specification says nothing about whether the reference implements it; the reference can be wrong in the same way as any implementation.
edges.missing: No independent executable reference exists; ETP-T5 is TODO and FRC-1 is open.

edges.obligation: The Rust implementation agrees with the executable reference at the declared interface, including failure behaviour, over a frozen input population.
edges.invalidation_rule: A change to the reference, the Rust implementation, or the differential harness invalidates it; the population is bound to the candidate identity.
edges.does_not_establish: Agreement on a finite input population is not a refinement proof; a passing differential court is not evidence about inputs outside the population or about failure behaviour it did not exercise.
edges.missing: There is no independent reference to compare against. The ETP-4 REDC congruence check compares two computations inside the same crate; the differential courts compare against the OpenSSL authority. Neither is an executable reference derived from the abstract specification.

edges.obligation: The observable C surface matches the contract: exported symbols and their versions, repr(C) layouts, ownership transfer and refcount conventions, error-queue classification and ordering, and callback semantics.
edges.discharged_by: ABI symbol, layout and version-script checks at the candidate
edges.invalidation_rule: A change to any exported symbol, repr(C) layout, error path or callback signature invalidates it; the contract must be re-measured at the new candidate.
edges.does_not_establish: Checking the exported symbol set and layouts does not establish ownership, error-queue ordering or callback semantics; an ABI match is not a semantic or memory-safety result.
bounded_population: the exported symbol set and the public layout probes at the candidate
edges.missing: Ownership, error-queue ordering and callback semantics are not established. OBL-MECH-C-ABI-CONTRACT (5 obligations) is NOT_ESTABLISHED, and OBL-XCUT-CALLBACKS is open. The parity model's OWNERSHIP_PASS, ERROR_PASS and STATE_PASS columns are not proved for the candidate.

edges.obligation: The exact compiled artefact implements the ABI contract and preserves the verified source properties, including the reassembly question.
edges.invalidation_rule: A change to the compiler, linker, assembler, target, profile or any build input invalidates it; no result carries across targets.
edges.does_not_establish: A proof about the source is not a proof about the binary; build reproducibility shows the binary is deterministic, not that it refines the source, and source-level constant-time intent is not binary timing.
edges.missing: No object-code correspondence exists. ETP-2 shows that two clean builds are byte-identical (archive 641471443209, measurement DSO 85395dcf7b76, distribution DSO 139966033ac9), which is a build-identity result. The branch audit is a review aid. ETP-T6 and FRC-4 are open.

edges.obligation: For every reachable call site c in the loaded DSO, Pre(c) implies the kernel precondition P, and Q satisfies the next consumer.
edges.discharged_by: consumer reachability closure at the loaded DSO
edges.invalidation_rule: A change to the DSO, the loader resolution or the consumer binary invalidates it; the closure is re-run at the new identities.
edges.does_not_establish: A reachability classification is not a memory-safety proof and not a SAFE_COMPATIBLE promotion; the closure's own non-claims state that a discharged obligation means an existing receipt covers a site, not that the site's precondition is established.
bounded_population: curl closure at fd25cc9e: 644 reachable files, 7/7 reachable production obligations
ssh closure at b85c: 625 reachable files, 290/290 reachable production obligations
edges.missing: The Pre(c) implication is not established at every reachable site. The b85c graduation is NOT_ESTABLISHED, both closures report safe_compatible=false, and the curl element-7 refusal population remains open (ETP-5 R5).

anti_implementation_shaped.rule: A specification artefact declares its refinement level and must not reference an internal identifier of the implementation level it refines: no internal function name, type name, field name or src/crate/super/self path.
anti_implementation_shaped.population_derivation: The distinct source documents of the T1 requirement nodes, union the contract documents named in the register.

inventory.would_close: Move the implementation-shaped residual statements into a review record and keep the requirement text independent of the type and function names.
Restate the standing standard in terms of the observable obligations and cite the adopted constructors from a review record, or record a reviewed exemption for each named identifier.
Restate each barrier in terms of its observable control and cite the mechanism from the T1 implementation nodes, or record a reviewed exemption.
Use the C-visible accessor convention rather than the wrapper method name, or record a reviewed exemption.
Use the C-visible ownership convention rather than the wrapper method name, or record a reviewed exemption.

anti_implementation_shaped.exemption_rule: A needed internal identifier may be named only through an exemption that records a justification, a reviewer and a review identity. An exemption that is incomplete is refused as unjustified; an exemption whose token no longer appears is refused as stale.
fail_closed: a population member that is neither registered, recorded as a known nonconformance, nor explicitly excluded
a specification with no declared level, or with a level outside the registry
an internal identifier inside a code span or a src/crate/super/self path
a known nonconformance whose token set changes or no longer reproduces
an unreadable register, an unreadable graph, or a duplicate JSON key
known_limits: Detection covers code spans and explicit source or Rust paths; an internal concept restated in prose without naming it is not detected.

The lexicon is a static scan of tracked src/**/*.rs and the exported-symbol records; a name that is both an authority observable and a Rust shim (OPENSSL_clear_free) is flagged by name and needs a reviewed exemption.
The guard checks naming, not semantic independence; a specification that rephrases the implementation in different words passes.

t1_projection.controls: forensics/tools/tests/test_traceability.py is 24/24; the three refinement orphan classes and the four refinement structural refusals each have a control.

non_claims: This architecture does not establish any refinement relation. Four of five edges are NONE or PARTIAL, and no edge is DISCHARGED.
A proof in a model is not a proof about the binary: no level above L4 has an object-code result.
A passing differential court is not a refinement proof: it is bounded to its population and its harness.
A reproducibility result is a build-identity result, not a source-to-binary refinement argument.
A consumer reachability closure is not a memory-safety proof and not a SAFE_COMPATIBLE promotion.
The anti-implementation-shaped guard checks naming, not semantic independence; a paraphrase in prose is outside its detection.
The known-nonconformance population is a recorded finding, not a licence: the five documents are not repaired by this item.
